text.title: Django Testing with pytest — Core Rules
text.summary: Ten testable rules every django-testing application must obey.

rule.statement: Configure pytest-django via pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] with an explicitly pinned DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE pointing at a dedicated test settings module (config.settings.test), addopts including --strict-markers, and testpaths. The settings module is never inferred from the environment.
rule.rationale: pyproject-as-single-source-of-truth eliminates pytest.ini/setup.cfg duplication and keeps lint+test config co-located. Pinning the settings module is the part that matters most: an inherited DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE means CI can run the suite against production settings, and the first thing that notices is the production database.

rule.statement: Use @pytest.mark.django_db (savepoint rollback) by default. Use @pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True) only when code calls on_commit or raw transactions.
rule.rationale: Savepoints are 5–10x faster than truncate-after-test; reserve transactional mode for code paths that actually depend on commit semantics.

rule.statement: Put shared fixtures in tests/conftest.py: api_client, authed_client, staff_client, and factory registrations. Never instantiate APIClient inside individual test functions.
rule.rationale: Centralised fixtures give one canonical client construction and let force_authenticate stay decoupled from the auth backend.

rule.statement: Create exactly one data-construction path per model: a Factory Boy factory registered via pytest_factoryboy.register (explicit), or `model_bakery.baker.make` (terse) — pick one per project. Use SubFactory for relationships, Faker for realistic data, LazyAttribute for derived fields, LazyFunction for independent computed values.
rule.rationale: Single factory prevents divergent defaults; pytest_factoryboy auto-creates instance and factory fixtures, eliminating manual fixture boilerplate.

rule.statement: Use DRF's APIClient with client.force_authenticate(user=user) for authed tests. Do not use credentials(HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=...) in view tests.
rule.rationale: force_authenticate bypasses token validation and tests the view logic only — switching auth backends does not break view tests.

rule.statement: Assert status code first, then assert specific response.data fields. Always use format='json'. Never rely solely on status_code == 200.
rule.rationale: A 200 with missing fields is a bug; asserting individual fields catches serializer drift and field renames.

rule.statement: Use @pytest.mark.parametrize to express permission matrices: (client_fixture, expected_status). One parametrized test replaces N nearly-identical tests.
rule.rationale: Combinatorial permission logic (roles × methods) is explicit and maintainable as a parametrize table; adding a role is one tuple, not a new function.

rule.statement: `Model.objects.create(...)` inline inside a test is forbidden. Every fixture object comes from the factory or from `baker.make`.
rule.rationale: Inline construction duplicates the model's required fields into every test file, so a single non-null field addition breaks dozens of unrelated tests at once and each one has to be edited by hand.

rule.statement: Service-layer tests invoke the real service, the real ORM and the real utils. Mocking is allowed ONLY at a process boundary: outbound HTTP, S3, a third-party SDK, the email backend. Mocking another function in the same codebase is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Mocking an internal collaborator tests the mock's contract, so a refactor that breaks the real call still passes. With savepoint rollback the real path is fast enough that the mock buys nothing but false confidence.

rule.statement: DRF endpoints are exercised with `rest_framework.test.APIClient`, never `django.test.Client`.
rule.rationale: The plain test client negotiates content differently, does not carry DRF authentication, and parses request bodies inconsistently — so the test either fails for reasons unrelated to the view, or passes against a request shape no real client sends.
